[Director 指令] [Patch — 重大改版] Venue 切换到 EMNLP 2026 (ARR)。8 页限制，当前 10 页需压缩 2 页。同时整合 5 个新分析结果。不用验证引用。

## 1. 压缩到 8 页（最高优先）

当前 10 页 main body + 4 页 appendix + 3 页 refs = 17 页。EMNLP 限制 8 页 main text + unlimited refs。

压缩策略：
- §4.4 Structural Analysis（plan_010 architecture + plan_021 non-uniform DIF）可大幅压缩或移入 appendix——architecture stratification 是 trivially null（99.98% decoder-only）
- §4.2 的 within-subject DIF 段可压缩——只保留 "5 subjects, avg 38.1%, robustness check" 一句
- Table 1 的 5 种 cohort 设计保留，但 Table 2 (threshold sensitivity) 可移入 appendix
- 精简 §5 Discussion

## 2. 整合新数据

**plan_024 (最重要)**：§4 或 §5 加 within-family ability-matched 分析
- Llama-2 vs 3: unmatched C%=61.3% → ability-matched C%=28.3%±1.6%
- Cohen's d=-0.99, overlap=0.18 (Llama) vs d=-0.17, overlap=0.66 (temporal cohort)
- 叙事：ability confound 解释约一半，但 28.3% 仍 substantial 且与 temporal 31.3% 量级一致
- 回应 reviewer 最关注的 ability confound 攻击

**Rank shift 分布**：§5 或 §4 反转叙事
- 全模型: median ΔRank=-3, IQR=75, 25% |ΔRank|≥100
- **修正误导措辞**：当前 "Phi-3/Llama-3 gain +700-850 ranks" 改为 family median/mean：
  "Llama-3 derivatives gain a median of +53 rank positions (mean +121), while Mistral-based models lose a median of 35 (mean -54)."
  Individual extremes (+793, -542) 可作为补充说明

**ΔFPR 代数证明**：§3 或 appendix
- Bootstrap CI = [0.000, 0.000]（5 subjects × 1000 resamples, 0/5000 non-zero）
- Cross-subject stratification scores 对 within-subject injection invariant → structural guarantee
- 一句话加入 §3 Method，详细证明可放 appendix

**LD×DIF 交叉**：§5 Discussion 一句话
- Extreme LD vs DIF C%: r=0.09 (p=0.50) — LD 不驱动 DIF
- Mean Q3 vs DIF C%: r=-0.36 (p=0.006) — 推理类 domain(low LD) DIF 更高
- 支持 "DIF captures items sensitive to capability evolution"

## 3. 引用修正
- 补 Clauser & Mazor (1998) + Nandakumar (1993) → §2/§3，定位 cross-subject matching 为 principled transfer
- 补 Carlini et al. (2022), Tirumala et al. (2022) → §2 LLM memorization
- 删除任何残留的 Tutz 引用（已确认不存在）

## 4. 叙事调整
- "Instability ≠ invalidity" framing 保留
- Model-specific rank shifts 提升为 diagnostic lens 主要证据（替代 GSM1K）
- GSM1K 保持 exploratory 标注
- 加 benchmark maintenance protocol 段（简短，3-4 句）：定期 DIF 监测建议 + item 分层标注 + cross-subject matching 作为标准 protocol

1	\section{Introduction}
2	\label{sec:introduction}
3	
4	When we say ``Model B outperforms Model A on MMLU,'' we implicitly assume that the benchmark measures the same construct in the same way for both models. This assumption of temporal comparability underpins every cross-generation comparison published on leaderboards and in model reports, yet it is rarely tested. We apply Mantel-Haenszel Differential Item Functioning (MH-DIF) analysis~\citep{holland1988mh} with Educational Testing Service (ETS) severity classification to the METABENCH response matrix~\citep{kipnis2024metabench}, and find that 31\% of MMLU~\citep{hendrycks2021mmlu} items receive ETS Category~C classification ($|\Delta_{\mathrm{MH}}| \geq 1.5$, $p < 0.05$), indicating large shifts in item functioning between models released in 2023 and 2024. This is not statistical noise: a random-split control within the 2023 cohort yields only 0.18\% ETS~C items. The instability persists across all 57 MMLU subjects (C\% range 21--48\%, unweighted mean $\approx 30\%$), and item-level regression shows that 92.4\% of this instability is unrelated to aggregate domain-level accuracy gains. Nearly one in three MMLU items behaves differently depending on when the evaluated models were trained. Crucially, this instability does not threaten benchmark validity: Spearman rank correlation between model rankings computed on all items versus stable-only items is $\rho \approx 0.997$. The instability is diagnostic, not destructive; it reveals which capability dimensions shift across model generations rather than rendering MMLU scores unreliable.
5	
6	A growing body of contamination detection research has produced sophisticated item-level methods, from membership inference approaches such as Min-K\%~\citep{shi2024mink} to performance-based detectors such as ConStat~\citep{dekoninck2024constat}, DVD~\citep{liang2026dvd}, and Self-Critique~\citep{tao2026selfcritique}. tool_args.new_string:
\paragraph{IRT in LLM Evaluation.}
IRT adoption in LLM evaluation has accelerated: \citet{lalor2019irt} introduced IRT to NLP, \citet{vania2021irt} assessed test set discriminability, and recent extensions include PSN-IRT \citep{zhou2026psnirt} for benchmark quality at scale and TinyBenchmarks \citep{maiapolo2024tinybenchmarks} for IRT-based item selection. The closest concurrent work is Growing Pains \citep{habba2026growingpains}, which addresses score comparability through fixed-parameter calibration \citep[FPC;][]{kim2019fpc}. Our work is complementary: Growing Pains assumes anchor item stability, while DIF analysis diagnoses which items violate this assumption.

tool_args.new_string:
\paragraph{Benchmark Design and Evaluation.}
Dynamic benchmarks such as Dynabench \citep{kiela2021dynabench}, LatestEval \citep{li2024latesteval}, and LiveBench \citep{white2025livebench} mitigate contamination by construction, yet none provides psychometric equating across versions. Chatbot Arena \citep{chiang2024chatbot} sidesteps static benchmarks through pairwise preference. Broader surveys \citep{chang2024survey, burnell2023rethink} identify benchmark saturation and lack of item-level transparency as systemic challenges. Our DIF analysis fills this gap by identifying which items have become unreliable for cross-generation comparison. METABENCH \citep{kipnis2024metabench} provides the large-scale response matrix that makes this analysis possible.

tool_args.old_string: Three progressively refined approaches (matched-ability quintiles, IRT $\theta$-conditioning, within-subject DIF) all fail to reduce the temporal FPR below 0.31. $\theta$-conditioning achieves $r(\theta, \mathrm{total\ score}) = 0.9986$ yet FPR $= 0.312$, and within-subject C\% $= 38.1\%$ exceeds the 25\% bifactor viability threshold. Yen's Q3 diagnostic reveals mild local dependence within subjects (11.3\% of pairs exceed $|Q3| > 0.20$, vs.\ 2.2\% cross-subject; $p = 2.3 \times 10^{-9}$), but cross-subject matching addresses this bias and temporal C\% persists. \Cref{app:structural} reports full results. As a further robustness check, logistic regression DIF on 9 MMLU subjects (1,787 items) confirms 92.1\% concordance between MH ETS~C and LR uniform DIF classifications and reveals additional non-uniform DIF (24.8\% of items at $|\beta_{\mathrm{interaction}}| \geq 0.5$) that MH is structurally unable to detect. The 31\% uniform DIF estimate is therefore conservative. A model independence sensitivity analysis addresses the concern that fine-tunes, merges, and quantizations inflate C\%: graduated de-duplication (limiting each family to $K$ models) yields C\% at or below size-matched random controls ($K{=}10$: 22.7\% vs.\ 26.8\%; $K{=}20$: 29.1\% vs.\ 30.9\%), confirming that family structure does not inflate the 31.3\% estimate.
tool_args.new_string: Three structural controls fail to reduce temporal C\% below 31\%: matched-ability quintiles, IRT $\theta$-conditioning ($r(\theta, \mathrm{total\ score}) = 0.9986$, FPR $= 0.312$), and within-subject DIF (C\% $= 38.1\%$, exceeding the 25\% bifactor viability threshold). Logistic regression DIF confirms 92.1\% concordance with MH and reveals additional non-uniform DIF (24.8\% at $|\beta_{\mathrm{interaction}}| \geq 0.5$), making the 31\% estimate conservative. Graduated de-duplication ($K{=}10$: 22.7\% vs.\ random 26.8\%; $K{=}20$: 29.1\% vs.\ 30.9\%) confirms family structure does not inflate C\%. Ability-matched within-family analysis reduces Llama-2 vs.\ Llama-3 C\% from 61.3\% (unmatched) to $28.3\% \pm 1.6\%$ (Cohen's $d = -0.99$, overlap $= 0.18$ vs.\ $d = -0.17$, overlap $= 0.66$ for temporal cohorts), indicating ability confounding explains roughly half; the residual 28.3\% is consistent with the temporal rate of 31.3\%. Full details in \Cref{app:structural}.

Within-subject matching on 5 representative subjects yields a mean of 38.1\% (range: 31--45\%), reported in \Cref{tab:temporal_landscape} as a robustness check for the matching protocol. Despite an ecological correlation of $\rho = 0.307$ ($p = 0.02$) between subject-level C\% and accuracy improvement, item-level logistic regression reveals that domain accuracy improvement explains only 2.4 percentage points of 31.3\% C\% (pseudo $R^2 = 0.0007$; counterfactual C\% $= 29.0\%$). tool_args.old_string: The near-chance enrichment (0.96) between DIF flags and web-overlap labels exposes a gap that extends beyond our analysis: all prior work validating item-level contamination detectors against web-overlap or $n$-gram labels conflates global exposure with differential functioning. Most MMLU items appear in web text, so web-overlap labels identify a condition shared by nearly all items rather than one that differentiates model cohorts. The enrichment of $\approx 1.0$ is the expected outcome when a differential method is evaluated against a global-exposure reference, not evidence of failure. The field needs validation methodologies that match the detection granularity: item-level differential detectors require item-level differential ground truth.
tool_args.new_string: The near-chance enrichment (0.96) between DIF flags and web-overlap labels exposes a broader gap: all prior work validating contamination detectors against web-overlap labels conflates global exposure with differential functioning. Most MMLU items appear in web text, so web-overlap labels identify a condition shared by nearly all items. The enrichment of $\approx 1.0$ is the expected outcome when a differential method is evaluated against a global-exposure reference. Item-level differential detectors require item-level differential ground truth.

tool_args.old_string: Three structural constraints limit DIF applicability in LLM benchmarks: (1) MMLU's multi-domain structure produces mild local dependence that elevates within-subject DIF rates (\Cref{sec:structural}); (2) reliable detection requires $N \geq 80$ per cohort and $|\Delta_{\mathrm{MH}}| \geq 1.4$; and (3) ability differences between temporal cohorts confound the DIF signal (within-family C\% $= 61.3\%$). A fourth limitation is that MH detects only uniform DIF; logistic regression analysis reveals additional non-uniform DIF (24.8\% at $|\beta_{\mathrm{interaction}}| \geq 0.5$; \Cref{sec:structural}), making the 31\% estimate conservative rather than exhaustive. Key limitations include the inability to distinguish contamination from legitimate capability change and limited benchmark scope (MMLU + GSM8K). DIF should be understood as a diagnostic lens for what changed across model generations, not a quality filter; LLM benchmarks need psychometric monitoring alongside score reporting.
tool_args.new_string:
Yen's Q3 analysis confirms that local dependence does not drive DIF: extreme LD correlates negligibly with subject-level C\% ($r = 0.09$, $p = 0.50$), while reasoning-heavy domains with low LD show higher DIF ($r = -0.36$, $p = 0.006$), consistent with DIF capturing items sensitive to capability evolution.

Structural constraints include: (1) reliable detection requires $N \geq 80$ per cohort; (2) ability differences confound the DIF signal (within-family C\% $= 61.3\%$, reduced to 28.3\% after ability matching); and (3) MH detects only uniform DIF, making the 31\% estimate conservative (24.8\% additional non-uniform DIF at $|\beta_{\mathrm{interaction}}| \geq 0.5$). Key limitations include inability to distinguish contamination from capability change and limited benchmark scope (MMLU + GSM8K).

These findings motivate a benchmark maintenance protocol: periodic DIF monitoring across model cohorts, item-level stability labels (stable/drifting/unstable) published alongside benchmark releases, and cross-subject matching as the standard protocol for semi-synthetic validation. DIF should be understood as a diagnostic lens, not a quality filter; LLM benchmarks need psychometric monitoring alongside score reporting.

tool_args.old_string:
\subsection{Cohort Designs}
\label{sec:cohorts}

DIF requires defining a reference group and a focal group. We construct five cohort comparisons, each designed to isolate a different source of variation.

\paragraph{Temporal.} The reference group consists of models released in 2023 ($N = 1{,}080$) and the focal group consists of models released in 2024 ($N = 807$). This is the primary comparison for detecting items whose functioning changed across model generations.

\paragraph{Ability-quintile.} Models within the same temporal window are divided by total score into quintiles. The focal group contains the lowest-scoring models (Q1--Q2) and the reference group contains the highest-scoring models (Q4--Q5). This comparison tests whether ability differences alone produce DIF, without temporal confounds.

\paragraph{Within-family.} Llama-2 models ($N = 161$) serve as the reference group and Llama-3 models ($N = 308$) as the focal group. This comparison isolates generational changes within a single model family.

\paragraph{Within-subject.} DIF is computed separately for each of the 57 MMLU subjects, with the matching variable (total score) restricted to items within the same subject. This design tests whether instability concentrates in specific knowledge domains.

\paragraph{Random split.} The 2023 cohort is divided into two equal random halves ($N = 540$ each). This serves as a sanity check: no systematic DIF should appear between two random subsets of the same population (expected C\% $\approx 0$).
